title: The reservoir at Langsett
summary: Drawn down in late summer, at which point the drowned road becomes available again for about six weeks.

body.text: For most of the year it is a reservoir. For a few weeks in a dry year it is a valley with a reservoir in the bottom of it, and a road going down into the water and out the other side.

The road served North America Farm, which is a real name and not a joke, and which was demolished along with everything else in the valley when the water came in 1904. In August of a dry year the drawdown exposes about three hundred metres of it: sett-laid, cambered, with the kerbs still in place, running out of the trees and straight into the water.
It is possible to walk on it. It is not possible to walk far. The surface is covered in a fine grey silt that holds a footprint perfectly and then loses it again the moment the level comes up.
The archive has visited in four consecutive years. The road was available in two of them.
